title: Spending Tracker — Full Stack
description: A production-grade personal finance platform with a Next.js dashboard, Spring Boot API, and Docker Compose deployment. Built end-to-end to replace subscription-based finance tools with a self-hosted, privacy-first alternative.
problem: Subscription-based personal finance tools lock users into monthly fees and third-party data access. Existing free alternatives feel like spreadsheet cosplay — slow, ugly, and missing real-time budget intelligence.
role: Solo architect and full-stack builder — frontend end-to-end, REST API design, database schema, DevOps pipeline, and production deployment.
outcome: Shipped a production-ready platform with auth, budget management, AI-powered insights, and dual-database support. Deployed via Netlify (frontend) and Docker Compose (full stack) with CI/CD versioned image builds.

title: Spending Tracker Backend
description: Spring Boot REST API serving the spending tracker frontend. Supports SQLite for solo users and MySQL for shared deployments from a single configuration flag — no code fork required.
problem: The frontend needed a stable, well-documented API that could run on SQLite for development and MySQL for production — without maintaining two codebases or complex migration scripts.
role: Solo backend engineer — API design, database abstraction layer, transaction categorization logic, budget math, and analytics aggregation endpoints.
outcome: Spring Boot service with full CRUD, JWT auth, budget calculations, and analytics endpoints. Same JAR runs against either database via environment config. Documented with OpenAPI specs.

title: Spending Tracker — DevOps & Deployment
description: One-command Docker Compose deployment that wires frontend, backend, databases, and reverse proxy. CI/CD pipeline builds and pushes versioned images on every Git tag.
problem: Hand-rolling deploys for a multi-service stack creates friction — env vars, network wiring, and image tags managed manually invites configuration drift and broken production deploys.
role: Solo DevOps engineer — containerization, compose orchestration, GitHub Actions workflow design, and production parity for local development.
outcome: One docker compose up brings the full stack online with persistent volumes, internal networking, and health checks. CI builds versioned multi-arch images and pushes to Docker Hub on every release tag.
